category: Guarded No-Op Ordering For Collection-Aligned Extension Scopes
description: Fix the no-profile guarded no-op path so unchanged writes with collection-aligned extension-scope rows short-circuit correctly after a prior collection reorder. Acceptance: `RelationalWriteNoProfileMergeSynthesizer` normalizes merged and current row ordering for `DbTableKind.CollectionExtensionScope` into the same deterministic stored/writable comparison order used by guarded no-op, instead of leaving merged aligned-scope rows in request traversal order while hydrated current rows remain in storage order; unchanged PUT and POST-as-update requests that touch a reordered base collection with aligned `_ext` rows return success as guarded no-ops and do not issue DML or bump `dms.Document.ContentVersion`; tests cover the case where base collection rows are reordered but aligned extension rows remain semantically unchanged.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests proving collection-aligned extension-scope `CurrentRows` and `MergedRows` compare equal for guarded no-op after a full-surface reorder when the aligned `_ext` data is unchanged.

Add PostgreSQL integration coverage for both an unchanged PUT and an unchanged POST-as-update against a previously reordered collection with aligned `_ext` rows, asserting unchanged table rows and unchanged `dms.Document.ContentVersion`.

description: Remove one-command-per-row delete behavior from stable-identity collection persistence. Acceptance: omitted collection/common-type/extension-collection rows are deleted through bounded parameterized batches or an equivalent chunked path that respects compiled batch limits on PostgreSQL and SQL Server; `RelationalWriteNonCollectionPersister` no longer loops over omitted collection rows and executes `DeleteByStableRowIdentitySql` once per row; delete-heavy updates continue to run inside the same transaction and preserve existing matched-row update, insert, and rollback behavior.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests that prove omitted stable-identity collection deletes are grouped into batched commands instead of one command per row on both PostgreSQL and SQL Server, including cases large enough to require multiple batches.
Add or update PostgreSQL integration coverage for a delete-heavy collection update and assert the final relational state remains correct after batched deletes.

description: Remove or wire up the unused executor diagnostic surface introduced during the DMS-984 refactor. Acceptance: `RelationalWriteExecutorRequest.DiagnosticIdentifier` is either deleted from the production contract and its redundant tests, or a concrete production consumer is added that justifies keeping it; no unused executor-facing request fields remain that are only asserted as null in tests; repository, executor, and seam tests are updated so the request contract reflects only inputs used by the current runtime path.
steps-to-verify: Search the backend and tests for `DiagnosticIdentifier` and update or delete all affected references so the contract matches actual runtime usage.
